rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The created things' differing colors are their varied forms, including green, white, red, and black.
rows.anchor: {مختلفا ألوانه} هيآته من خضرة وبياض وحمرة وسواد وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: أكثر التفاسير
rows.claim: Most exegetes coordinate “what He has created” with night and day, taking it as another thing subjected for people.
rows.anchor: وفي أكثر التفاسير وما ذرأ معطوف على الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says creation for people makes mention of subjection redundant; the answer is that creation does not logically guarantee accessibility, since what is created for people may remain hard to obtain.
rows.anchor: واعتذر بأن الأول لا يستلزم الثاني لزوما عقليا لجواز كون ما خلق لهم عزيز المرام صعب المنال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The described acts of subjection and creation show that their agent is one, with no partner; recognizing this sign requires recalling necessary knowledge.
rows.anchor: دالة على أن من هذا شأنه واحد لا شريك له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, night is human nature, day is spirituality, the sun is spirit, the moon is heart, and the stars are the powers and five senses.
rows.anchor: {والشمس} شمس الروح {والقمر} قمر القلب {والنجوم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward subjection of these faculties means using them according to the Sacred Law and the Sufi path, under the care of an adept spiritual physician.
rows.anchor: وهو خطاب وتسخيرها استعمالها على وفق الشريعة وقانون الطريقة بمعالجة طبيب حاذق

words: إن فى ذالك لايات لقوم يعقلون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who reason through signs of the Real reach direct witnessing without discursive reflection.
rows.anchor: بشواهد الحق من غير التفكر بل بالمعاينات

words: وما ذرأ لكم فى الأرض مختلفا ألوانه
rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The earth is the constitution's ground, and its diverse colors signify the angelic, satanic, and animal capacities within human beings.
rows.anchor: في أرض جبلتكم من الاستعدادات

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Souls pass through different worlds and take on each world's color, moving among angelic, satanic, and animal realms until returned to the lowest bodily form.
rows.anchor: عبور أرواحهم على هذه العوالم المختلفة وتلونها في كل عالم بلون ذلك العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A discerning person should escape heedlessness and bind himself to the people of remembrance.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يتخلص من قيد الغفلة ويربط نفسه بسلسلة أهل التذكر

rows.speaker: محمد بن فضل
rows.claim: Remembrance by the tongue brings expiations and ranks, while remembrance of the heart brings nearness and intimacy; recollection belongs to the heart, which commands the body yet is captive to God.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن فضل : ذكر اللسان كفارات ودرجات

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The report says that if devils did not hover over human hearts, people would see the kingdom of the heavens.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "لولا أن الشياطين يحومون على قلوب بني آدم لنظروا إلى ملكوت السموات"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report points to the causes that veil the heart from the unseen kingdom.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه إشارة إلى الأسباب التي هي حجاب بين القلب وبين الملكوت

rows.speaker: الخالصة
rows.claim: People of inward life fall into three classes: beastlike hearts, human bodies with satanic spirits, and those sheltered by God on the day when there is no shade but His.
rows.anchor: وأصحاب القلوب من الانس ثلاثة صنف كالبهائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is spherical and lies at the world's center; its name is linked to the verb for consuming, since it consumes human bodies.
rows.anchor: هي كروية الشكل محلها وسط العالم وسميت بالأرض لأنها تأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God set firm mountains in the earth without support, picturing them as pebbles cast by a hand to portray divine greatness and power over every difficult thing.
rows.anchor: جبالا ثوابت من غير سبب ولا ظهير كأنها حصيات قبضهن قابض بيده فنبذهن في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rawāsi means firmly settled mountains; it is the plural of rāsiyah, with a feminine ending because it describes mountains.
rows.anchor: من رسا الشيء إذا نبت جمع راسية والتاء للتأنيث على أنها صفة جبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is an object of purpose; mayd means movement or swaying, and the earth's being anchored is to prevent it from shaking people.
rows.anchor: الميد الحركة والميل يقال ما ديميد ميدا تحرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth was created unstable on water, then God anchored it with mountains according to His customary ordering of things through causes; Bursevī gives their number as 6,673, excluding hills.
rows.anchor: وقد خلق الله الأرض مضطربة لكونها على الماء ثم أرساها بالجبال وهي ستة آلاف وستمائة وثلاثة وسبعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains support the earth as bones support an animal's body; he compares this with the soothsayer Satih, whose body lacked bones except the tailbone and could not hold itself upright.
rows.anchor: فالأرض بلا جبال كاللحم بلا عظام فكما أن وجود الحيوان وجسده إنما يستمسك بالعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anhar is the plural of nahr, also pronounced nahar, and means a watercourse; the word “cast” also carries the sense of making, so rivers were made in the earth.
rows.anchor: جمع نهر ويحرك مجرى الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates the rivers with the Euphrates at Kufa, Tigris at Baghdad, Jayhun at Balkh, Jeyhan at Adana, Sihon in India, Saihan at al-Massisa, and the Nile in Egypt.
rows.anchor: مثل الفرات نهر الكوفة ودجلة نهر بغداد وجيحون نهر بلخ وجيحان نهر اذنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subul is the plural of sabil, meaning roads or clear ways.
rows.anchor: وطرقا مختلفة جمع سبيل وهو الطريق وما وضح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of making roads is that people may find their destinations and dwellings.
rows.anchor: إرادة أن تهتدوا بها إلى مقاصدكم ومنازلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent a particular messenger to each nation, as He sent Muhammad to his community.
rows.anchor: رسولا} خاصا بهم كما بعثناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle an explains the sending: God instructed each messenger to tell his people to worship Him alone.
rows.anchor: أن مفسرة لبعثنا أي : قلنا لهم على لسان الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commanded worship is worship of God alone.
rows.anchor: على لسان الرسول اعبدوا الله وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taghut is Satan and everything that calls people toward error.
rows.anchor: هو الشيطان وكل ما يدعوا إلى الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship God and avoid taghut completes the proof and removes excuses, despite God's knowing some will disobey and disbelieve.
rows.anchor: وذلك لإلزام الحجة وقطع المعذرة مع علمه أن منهم من لا يأتمر بالأوامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taghut follows the pattern faʿalūt like jabarūt and malakūt; its source form is ṭugh-yūt, with the lām moved before the ʿayn and an extra tāʾ that is not feminine.
rows.anchor: والطاغوت فعلوت من الطغيان كالجبروت والملكوت من الجبر والملك وأصله طغيوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Minhum refers to the nations, and the fāʾ supplies an understood consequence: after the messengers delivered their charge, the people divided.
rows.anchor: أي : من تلك الأمم والفاء فصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates guidance to the truth in those who are guided, after they direct their partial power and choice toward worship and avoiding taghut.
rows.anchor: خلق فيه الاهتداء إلى الحق الذي هو عبادته واجتناب الطاغوت بعد صرف قدرتهم واختيارهم الجزئي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misguidance becomes fixed until death because of defiance and persistence; God does not create guidance in such a person or will to purify the person's heart.
rows.anchor: أي : وجبت وثبتت إلى حين الموت لعناده وإصراره عليها وعدم صرف قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to travel and observe addresses the Quraysh; the immediate fāʾ signals that they should promptly reflect and infer, so they leave error.
rows.anchor: وفي الفاء الموضوعة للتعقيب إشارة إلى وجوب المبادرة إلى النظر والاستدلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh should take warning from the destroyed homes and traces of ʿĀd, Thamud, and others who followed their way.
rows.anchor: من عاد وثمود ومن سار بسيرتهم ممن حقت عليه الضلالة لعلكم تعتبرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even Muhammad's earnest effort cannot produce guidance by compulsion: God does not create forced guidance in one whom He lets stray for choosing badly.
rows.anchor: أي : فاعلم أن الله لا يخلق الهداية جبرا وقهرا فيمن يخلق فيه الضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ummahāt is the plural of umm (mother), with an added hāʾ, as in ihraq from araq.
rows.anchor: جمع الأم زيدت الهاء فيها كما زيدت في الإهراق من أراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At birth people know nothing of worldly or afterlife matters, including what their souls knew in the spirit world, what their atoms knew at the primordial covenant, or the innate skills animals display when seeking their mothers and food.
rows.anchor: أي : حال كونكم غير عالمين شيئا أصلا من أمور الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdi's couplet contrasts an ant that emerges from its egg and seeks food with a human born without awareness, reason, or discernment.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ سعدي قدس سره : مر غك از بيضه برون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing is mentioned before sight because it receives revelation and because some prophets lost sight but not hearing; alternatively, hearing develops before sight, as a newborn's eyes open later.
rows.anchor: قدمه على البصر لما أنه طريق تلقى الوحي ولذا ابتلي بعض الأنبياء بالعمى دون الصمم أو لأن إدراكه أقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samʿ is singular because it was originally a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وإفراده باعتبار كونه مصدرا في الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Absār is the plural of baṣar, the sense of the eye.
rows.anchor: جمع بصر وهي محركة حس العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afʾidah is the plural of fuʾād, the heart's center; it relates to the heart as the heart relates to the chest.
rows.anchor: جمع فؤاد وهو وسط القلب وهو من القلب كالقلب من الصدر

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Although afʾidah is a small-number plural, it serves for abundance here and in similar verses because the address “for you” is general.
rows.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" : استعملت في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These faculties are instruments for knowledge: the senses register particulars, and the heart notices similarities and differences through repeated sensations, enabling new and acquired knowledge.
rows.anchor: جعل لكم هذه الأشياء آلات تحصلون بها العلم والمعرفة بأن تحسوا بمشاعركم جزئيات الأشياء

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: The conjunction with “He brought you out” joins the events without fixing their order; the faculties' effects appear only after birth, though they already existed potentially.
rows.anchor: وليس فيه دلالة على تأخر الجعل المذكور عند الإخراج لما أن مدلول الواو هو الجمع مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He arranges seven divine attributes—life, knowledge, will, power, hearing, sight, and speech—and relates the sequence of human development from hearing through sight to speech to this pattern of perfection.
rows.anchor: تعالى صفات سبعا مرتبة وهي الحياة والعلم والإرادة والقدرة والسمع والبصر والكلام

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report forbids a believer from impregnating another man's already occupied field; Bursevī invokes it in discussing a pregnant woman's marriage.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر لا يسقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marriage to a pregnant woman is forbidden when pregnancy comes from a lawful marriage; the ruling for pregnancy from illicit sex is disputed.
rows.anchor: ولذا حرم تزوج الحبلى من النكاح اتفاقا ومن الزنى اختلافا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says a fetus's hearing and sight become sharper through intercourse, supporting the discussion of prenatal faculties.
rows.anchor: قلنا قد جاء في الخبر "إن سمع الحمل وبصره يزداد حده بالوطىء"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude means using hearing for God's speech, the Prophet's reports, and the wisdom of saints, and using sight to read God's signs and infer His existence, unity, knowledge, and power; misuse betrays His trusts.
rows.anchor: وشكرها استعمالها فيما خلقت لأجله من استماع كلام الله وأحاديث رسول الله وحكم أوليائه

rows.speaker: الشيخ السعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdi's verses urge careful listening to the Qur'an and avoiding falsehood, and praise attending to the Creator's artistry while overlooking a brother's faults.
rows.anchor: كذر كاه قرآن وندس كوش به بهتان وباطل شنيدن مكوش

rows.speaker: صائب
rows.claim: The cited couplet calls the heart a trustee and warns against sleeping while God's trust is exposed to thieves.
rows.anchor: وقال الصائب : ترابكو هردل كرده اند امانتدار

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: At the bodily level humans receive senses like animals; their spirits receive hearing, sight, and understanding like angels; their innermost secrets hear, see, and know through God.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {وجعل لكم السمع والابصار والافادة}

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The cited sacred report says God becomes the servant's hearing, sight, and tongue, through which the servant hears, sees, and speaks.
rows.anchor: كنت له سمعا وبصرا ولسانا فبي يسمع وبي يبصر وبي ينطق

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Gratitude for these faculties means using them to seek God, looking past the gifts to the Giver.
rows.anchor: وأداء شكر نعم الله باستعمالها وصرفها في طلب الله وترك الالتفات إلى النعم بل للمنعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mothers' wombs signify nonexistence, the true mother; before God taught all names, people knew nothing.
rows.anchor: أي : من العدم وهو الأم الحقيقي لا تعلمون شيئا قبل أن يعلمكم الله أسماء كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the primordial address “Am I not your Lord?”, God's disclosure of lordship gave them a tongue, through the light of His hearing, to answer “Yes.”
rows.anchor: حين خاطبكم بقوله : ألست بربكم فتجلى لكم بروبوبيته فبنور سمعه أعطاكم لسانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward gratitude is to hear only God's speech, see only His beauty, love only His essence, and speak only with Him.
rows.anchor: فلا تسمعون بهذا السمع إلا كلامه ولا تبصرون بهذا البصر إلا جماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about birds urges observers to reflect and be astonished at them as evidence of God's power.
rows.anchor: تقرير لمن ينظر إليهن وتعجيب من شأنهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birds are made compliant for flight through wings and other helpful means.
rows.anchor: مذللات للطيران بما خلق لها من الأجنحة والأسباب المساعدة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording intensifies the wonder: subjection usually means one party controls another, yet here air is subjected to birds, whose natural tendency would be to fall.
rows.anchor: والواقع هنا تسخير الهواء للطير لتطير فيه كيف تشاء فكان مقتضى طبيعة الطير السقوط

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses saw a green tree encircled from base to top by brilliantly burning white fire, with no person nearby; neither the fire dimmed the tree nor the tree's water dimmed the fire.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : رأى شجرة خضراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses heard the angels glorifying God, saw a light too intense for eyes, covered his eyes, and was overcome with fear and astonishment before calm was sent upon him.
rows.anchor: فسمع تسبيح الملائكة ورأى نورا عظيما تكل الأبصار عنه فوضع يديه على عينيه وخاف وبهت

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: The tree is identified variously as a green samura, an ʿawsaja, a blackberry-like thorn tree, or a jujube; these trees contain no fire unlike other trees.
rows.anchor: وكانت الشجرة سمرة خضراء أو عوسجة أو عليقا أو شجرة العناب وهي شجرة لا نار فيها

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: One four-part classification says worldly fire eats but does not drink, green-tree fire drinks but does not eat, Hellfire both eats and drinks, and Moses' fire neither eats nor drinks.
rows.anchor: قالوا : النار أربعة أصناف : صنف يأكل ولا يشرب

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: A second classification distinguishes fire with burning but no light (Hell), light without burning (Moses), both (worldly fire), and neither (trees).
rows.anchor: وقالوا أيضا هي أربعة أنواع : نوع له إحراق بلا نور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, light signifies love and fire signifies ardent love; when Moses' love and longing were full, the essential light appeared in the form of attribute-fire, burned away his selfhood, and brought single-hearted orientation.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : النور للمحبة والنار للعشق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated pronouns stress certainty: Moses is told to have no doubt that the speaker is his Lord.
rows.anchor: للتوكيد والتحقق يعني (شك مكن ومتيقن شوكه من)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Removing the sandals is commanded because going barefoot better expresses humility and proper decorum before God.
rows.anchor: أمر بذلك لأن الحفوة أدخل في التواضع وحسن الأدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bishr al-Hafi and other pious predecessors walked barefoot, and earlier generations circumambulated the Kaaba barefoot.
rows.anchor: ولذلك كان بشر الحافي ونحوه يسيرون حفاة وكان السلف الصالحون يطوفون بالكعبة حافين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says Moses' bare feet honor the holy valley by his arrival and connect its blessing to him.
rows.anchor: ليتشرف مشهد الوادي بقدوم قدميه وتتصل بركة الأرض إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another says the Beloved was told to approach the Throne's carpet in sandals so the Throne would be honored by their dust and its light would reach him; this applies to Muhammad's rank, unlike Moses' station.
rows.anchor: وقيل للحبيب تقدم على بساط العرش بنعليك ليتشرف العرش بغبار نعال قدميك

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: A report about Abū Ḥanīfa says that when he visited the caliph, the caliph asked him to stay mounted and tread on the caliph's carpet with his mule.
rows.anchor: وذكر في فضائل أبي حنيفة أنه كان إذا قدم على الخليفة للزيارة

rows.speaker: حل الرموز
rows.claim: One explanation says the sandals were made of untanned donkey hide, making the command a matter of decorum.
rows.anchor: أو لأنهما كانا غير مدبوغين من جلد الحمار فالخطاب خطاب التأديب كما في "حل الرموز"

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kāshifī considers it more correct that the sandals were made of processed, ritually pure cowhide.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (أصح آنست كه نعلين از جلد بقربود وطاهر)

rows.speaker: الأسرار المحمدية
rows.claim: A dream interpretation takes the sandals to mean a man's wife; another commentary glosses removing them as setting aside concern for wife and sheep.
rows.anchor: قال في "الأسرار المحمدية" جاء في غرائب التفسير في قوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: الشيخ افتاده
rows.claim: Sheikh Aftade interprets the sandals as nature and the self; Bursevī agrees that wife represents nature, child the self, and sheep livelihood, so Moses is told to leave all such concerns behind.
rows.anchor: وقال حضرة الشيخ الشهير بافتاده قدس سره يعني الطبيعة والنفس

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the two sandals signify this world and the next, so Moses is ordered to become wholly absorbed in knowing and beholding God.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : "المراد بالنعلين الدنيا والآخرة كأنه أمره بالاستغراق

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others take the sandals as the two premises proving a Creator: once one reaches knowledge of God, one should stop attending to the proof and remain absorbed in sacred light.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن إثبات الصانع يكون بمقدمتين فشبهتا بالنعلين إذ بهما يتوصل

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: Rūmī's cited verse begins an analogy about reaching the roof of heaven, which makes the search for a ladder unnecessary.
rows.anchor:
وفي "المثنوي" :
ون شدى ربامهاى آسمان

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: Rūmī says that once the clear mirror of realization is polished, polishing it further is ignorance, just as seeking a messenger's letter is ugly before a welcoming king.
rows.anchor: آينه روشن كه شد صاف وجلى

rows.speaker: الشبلي
rows.claim: After reaching God, al-Shiblī washed all his books, illustrating that discursive proofs are left behind after realization.
rows.anchor: غسل حضرة الشيخ الشبلي قدس سره جميع كتبه بعد الوصول إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sanctified valley is pure and set apart from evil.
rows.anchor: {إنك بالواد المقدس} المطهر والمتبعد من السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tuwa is an appositive proper name for the valley; with tanwin it is declined as a place name, while without it it is indeclinable as a known region.
rows.anchor: {طوى} اسم الوادي عطف بيان له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Moses removed his sandals and cast them beyond the valley.
rows.anchor: روي أن موسى عليه السلام خلعهما وألقاهما وراء الوادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose Moses, selecting him for prophethood and messengership.
rows.anchor: {وأنا اخترتك} أي : اصطفيتك للنبوة والرسالة

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads the verb in the plural form, “We chose you,” instead of “I chose you.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة "وأنا اخترناك"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is told to listen attentively to the command and prohibition revealed by God.
rows.anchor: للذي يوحى إليك مني من الأمر والنهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is attached to the verb of hearing as an added preposition before its object, as in “radifa lakum.”
rows.anchor: اللام متعلقة بالسمع مزيدة في المفعول كما في ردف لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is to go to Pharaoh and his chiefs by way of preaching and warning, carrying the staff and the hand as his two signs.
rows.anchor: اذهب} يا موسى بطريق الدعوة والتحذير {إلى فرعون} وملئه بهاتين الآيتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two proofs are identified as Moses' staff and hand; Bursevī cites the explicit description in al-Qaṣaṣ.
rows.anchor: لقوله تعالى في سورة القصص {فذانك برهانان من ربك إلى فرعون وملايه}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī postpones explaining why another verse uses the plural “My signs” until its later discussion.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله تعالى : {اذهب أنت وأخوك بااياتى} (طه : 42)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh exceeded the bounds of servitude by claiming divinity independently, not as a partner, as in his claim “I am your highest lord.”
rows.anchor: أي : جاوز حد العبودية بدعوى الربوبية استقلالا لا اشتراكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a sincere wayfarer reaches completion, God appoints him to guide and train other servants.
rows.anchor: أن السالك الصادق إذا بلغ مرتبة كماله يقيضه الله لدلالة عباده وتربيتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mature return to mix with people and endure their harm, thereby testing their forbearance and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: أن كمال البالغين في أن يرجعوا إلى الخلق ومخالطتهم والصبر على أذاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff was appropriate because it is a shepherd's tool and Moses had been a shepherd.
rows.anchor: لأن العصا من آلات الرعاة وموسى عليه السلام كان راعيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī crudely likens Pharaoh to a donkey that required a staff and beating; Rūmī's cited verses elaborate this image of correction and warning.
rows.anchor: الحمار فاحتاج إلى العصا والضرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing the task was heavy and immense, Moses sought God's support in prayer because he feared he could not withstand Pharaoh and his army alone.
rows.anchor: موسى مستعينا بالله لما علم أنه حمل ثقيل وتكليف عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “breast” means the heart, not the physical chest; Moses asks for a heart broad enough to withstand opponents' foolishness, obstinacy, power, and numbers without fear.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالصدر هنا القلب لا العضو الذي فيه القلب

rows.speaker: شيخي وسندي
rows.claim: Bursevī says his spiritual master recounted being commanded in a midmorning dream in Filibe to migrate to Constantinople; after waking, praying, and washing, he left on foot and left his family behind.
rows.anchor: وسمعت من شيخي وسندي قدس سره أنه نام نومة الضحى يوما في مدينة فلبه

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Hāfiẓ's couplet longs for the day of leaving this station, when companions will ask for news from the beloved's street.
rows.anchor:
قال الحافظ :
387
خرم آن روزكه زين مرحله بربندم رخت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual address either uses grammatical predominance or comes after Moses and Aaron have met; the repeated command sets up what follows.
rows.anchor: هذا الخطاب إما بطريق التغليب أو بعد ملاقاة أحدهما الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh is a foreign name and title for al-Walīd ibn Muṣʿab; the word generated a verb for acting like Pharaoh, and tyrants are called pharaohs and devils.
rows.anchor: وفرعون اسم أعجمي لقب الوليد بن مصعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭughyān is exceeding the limit in disobedience; Pharaoh exceeded servitude by claiming divinity.
rows.anchor: الطغيان مجاوزة الحد في العصيان أي : تجاوز حد العبودية

rows.speaker: العرائس
rows.claim: God sent Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh to cut off his argument and expose the falsehood of his claim; this warns every claimant who lacks proof from God.
rows.anchor: قال في "العرائس" : أمر الله موسى وهارون عليهما السلام بالذهاب إلى فرعون

rows.speaker: العرائس
rows.claim: Sending prophets to enemies teaches them their inability to guide others or even themselves, like a doctor who cannot treat others and cannot treat himself.
rows.anchor: والحكمة في إرسال الأنبياء إلى الأعداء ليعرفوا عجزهم عن هداية الخلق إلى الله

rows.speaker: العرائس
rows.claim: The mission teaches prophets that divine election does not arise from worldly causes and should make them grateful; it may also draw prepared believers out from among unbelievers, such as Habib al-Najjar, Pharaoh's relative and wife, and the magicians.
rows.anchor: وليعلموا أن الاختصاص لا يكون بالأسباب ويشكروا الله بما أنعم عليهم بلطفه

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says Pharaoh was in truth sent to the magicians: God sends prophets to enemies to draw His believing friends out of their midst.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : الإشارة إلى فرعون وهو المبعوث بالحقيقة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The mission's benefit returned to Moses and Aaron, not Pharaoh: their messengership and warning would be established, while Pharaoh's denial would make his disbelief manifest, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" اعلم أن فائدة إتيانهما ورسالتهما إلى فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should address Pharaoh gently and kindly, without roughness or scolding; gentleness adorns whatever enters it, while harshness mars it.
rows.anchor: كلماه باللين والرفق من غير خشونة ولا تعنيف ويسرا ولا تعسرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was sharp and hard-tempered, becoming so angry that his cap seemed to catch fire; gentleness was prescribed to soften his temper and make him forbearing.
rows.anchor: وكان في موسى حدة وصلابة وخشونة بحيث إذا غضب اشتعلت قلنسوته نارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view contrasts Muhammad's gentle and merciful temperament, which suited the command to severity, with Moses' hard and forceful temperament, which suited the command to gentleness; each completes a different divine quality.
rows.anchor: طبع الحبيب كان على اللين والرحمة فلذا أمر بالغلظة كما قال تعالى : {واغلظ عليهم}

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The prophetic maxim “Adopt God's qualities” supports embodying both majesty and beauty in the manner suited to each prophet's station.
rows.anchor: وقد قال عليه السلام : "تخلقوا بأخلاق الله"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh was a tyrannical king who would grow more defiant under harsh admonition; gentleness was safer and more effective, while sternness can suit the common people.
rows.anchor: وأيضا إن فرعون كان من الملوك الجبابرة ومن عادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harsh words might have provoked Pharaoh to strike or kill Moses, so gentleness also protected Moses.
rows.anchor: فلو كان في قول موسى خشونة لم يحتمل طبع فرعون بل هاج غضبه فلعله يقصد موسى بضرب أو قتل

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: At the beginning of a mission, the preacher should give the addressee room to consider the message; only after defiance and obstinacy do harshness and severity become appropriate.
rows.anchor: وفي "الأسئلة المقحمة" إنما أمرهما بذلك لأنه كان ابتداء حال الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gentleness and sternness can each be praised or blamed depending on circumstances; sound judgment follows what the situation requires and avoids either extreme.
rows.anchor: فكل من اللين والخشونة يمدح به طورا ويذم به طورا بحسب اختلاف الواقع
